note: Every runner label maps to an AWS Intel instance family (e.g. c7i, m6i). AWS capacity is donated credits from Amazon to the LF's AWS account, not LF's own money; Meta's own AWS-hosted usage is funded by Meta directly.

AWS AMD instance families (c6a, c5a, ...) are donated Amazon credits, not LF's own money. GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest/ubuntu-22.04 runners (Azure-hosted) are funded by Meta only -- LF has no current involvement in GitHub-hosted runner spend.

GitHub-hosted runner labels with no instance family in the FOCUS export to identify the exact CPU; GitHub-hosted runners run on Azure and are funded by Meta only -- LF has no current involvement here.
Graviton is an AWS-only instance family. AWS capacity is donated Amazon credits, not LF's own money; Meta's own AWS-hosted usage is funded by Meta directly.
GitHub-hosted Arm images (ubuntu-*-arm, windows-11-arm); GitHub-hosted runners run on Azure and are funded by Meta only -- LF has no current involvement here.

AWS (g4dn/g5/p-family) capacity is donated Amazon credits, not LF's own money; Meta's own AWS-hosted usage is funded by Meta directly. DGX-labeled runners (linux.dgx.b200) and rtx-40x0/50x0-* runners are both Nvidia-hosted and Nvidia-funded -- the RTX ones serve NVIDIA's own out-of-tree Windows CI. A subset of labels (linux.gcp.*, gcp-*-runner) indicate GCP-hosted capacity whose funder is still unconfirmed, and a few (a100-runner, B200, a.linux.b200.2) name no identifiable host at all.

AMD-donated capacity; cost is an estimate derived from GPU-hours x a per-GPU multiplier, not billing data. Runner labels name the host directly (amd-sandbox-linux-doks.* = DigitalOcean Kubernetes, amd-vtr-*/*.vultr.test = Vultr). Some labels (*.meta-pytorch, *.ecosystem.*) indicate which org schedules work on this AMD-donated hardware, not who funded it -- Funded By reflects the funder, not the scheduler.

Most XPU hours are Intel test jobs carved out of LF's/Meta's own AWS-hosted runners by job-name matching (see redistribute_intel_jobs_to_xpu() in render.py) -- that AWS capacity is donated Amazon credits (for LF's portion) or Meta's own spend (for Meta's portion), not Intel hardware. A smaller portion is genuinely Intel-hosted and Intel-funded (linux.client.xpu, linux.ril.xpu, linux.hpu.gaudi3.8).
